The egg positions touch according to grid adjacency relationships: two adjacent egg positions in the same row will touch, and two vertically adjacent egg positions in the same column will also touch. raw_record.question_text: A hen lays white and brown eggs. Lisa takes six of them and puts them in a box as shown. The brown eggs are not allowed to touch each other. What is the maximum number of brown eggs Lisa can place in the box?

method.method_draft: First read the image as a 2-by-3 egg box: six circular egg positions arranged in two rows and three columns. Positions that share a side in this grid are touching: horizontal neighbors in the same row touch, and vertical neighbors in the same column touch. From the text, brown eggs may not touch each other, and the task is to maximize the number of brown positions. Model the six positions as a 2x3 grid graph and choose a largest set of non-adjacent cells. A checkerboard choice such as top-left, top-right, and bottom-middle gives 3 brown eggs with no touching. Four is impossible because in each of the three columns at most one egg can be brown, and trying to choose from all three columns already forces the checkerboard maximum; equivalently the largest independent set of a 2x3 grid is 3. Therefore the maximum is 3.
